title: MITM via ARP Spoofing
description: Mermaid sequence diagram of a man-in-the-middle attack via ARP cache poisoning: the normal ARP and HTTP flow, the attacker's gratuitous ARP replies, the resulting relayed flow, and the HTTPS defense that defeats it.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: Network Security Foundations: Protocols, Firewalls, and Detection

educational.topic: ARP cache poisoning and man-in-the-middle attacks
learningObjectives: Describe how an attacker uses gratuitous ARP replies to poison the client and gateway ARP caches.
Trace how poisoned caches place the attacker on the path between client and gateway.
Explain why HTTPS with proper certificate validation defeats the impersonation.
educational.prerequisites: Basic understanding of IP/MAC addressing and how ARP resolves an IP to a MAC.

controls: Read the autonumbered messages top to bottom
Phase notes mark normal flow, attack begins, and after-poisoning flow
pedagogical.assessment: Students identify which two ARP replies poison which caches, and explain why the gateway also needs to be poisoned (not just the client).
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing ARP spoofing alone lets an attacker read HTTPS content.
Assuming only the client's cache needs to be poisoned for a full MITM.
